COMMON ORDER Dt: 10.05.2024 (per Hon'ble Sri Justice R.Raghunandan Rao)
These two writ petitions are being disposed of by way of a present common order as they relate to the same piece of land and challenge essentially the same proceedings of the official respondents.
2. Heard Sri M.L. Ali and Sri S. Sree Rama Chandra Murthy, learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Government Pleader for land Acquisition, appearing for the respondents.
3. W.P.No.8542 of 2006 was filed by nine persons.
The 1st petitioner claims to be the owner of 69 cents of land in R.S.No.63/6 of Prasadampadu, Vijayawada Rural Mandal, Krishna District.
Petitioners 2 to 9 are said to be the tenants of the 1st petitioner.
This fact is admitted by the 1st petitioner in his affidavit.

In 1994, the HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 Sub Collector, Vijayawada initiated land acquisition proceedings for acquiring the aforesaid land for the purpose of construction of a telephone exchange building.
On 05.07.1994, necessary notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was published in the A.P. Gazette.
Subsequently, substance of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was also published in two local newspapers on 15.07.1994.
A notice under Section 5-A of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 17.09.1994 and an enquiry was conducted there on.

After completion of the said enquiry, a declaration under Section 6 was published in the Gazette on 05.05.1995 and the substance of the said declaration was also published in two Telugu daily news papers on 01.06.1995.

At that stage, about 19 persons approached the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh,
by way of W.P.No.26001 of 1995 claiming that their possession and enjoyment of the said 69 cents was being disturbed by the official respondents without following the process and procedure laid down under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
On 24.11.1995, a direction was issued in the above writ petition directing the official respondents therein not to dispossess the petitioners from the land without following due process of law.

Thereafter, there was absolute silence on the part of the official respondents which is said to have forced the 1st HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 &
34189 of 2022 petitioner herein to file W.P.No.16682 of 2003 seeking a direction of early completion of the land acquisition proceedings.

The erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, by way of interlocutory proceedings dated 23.09.2003 directed the official respondents to complete the land acquisition proceedings within a period of six weeks.

As no action was being taken against this Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129136886/
2 direction, a contempt notice was given by the 1st petitioner to the official respondents to implement the orders dated 23.09.2003, issued by the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh.

sentences.text: 4. The petitioners having waited for quite some time for completion of the land acquisition proceedings, finally moved the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh by way of W.P.No.8542 of 2006 for a declaration that the land acquisition proceedings initiated on 03.06.1994 had fallen foul of Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act and the entire process has to be set aside.
After receipt of this notice, the Sub Collector, Vijayawada deposited an amount of Rs.7,65,515/- on 26.04.2006 before the Civil Court, Vijayawada.

Thereafter, the 3rd respondent Sub-Collector filed a counter affidavit stating that an award had been passed on 20.05.1997 and as such, the entire land acquisition proceedings had been completed within the time mandated under Section 11-A of the HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 Land Acquisition Act and as such, none of the proceedings have lapsed.
5.
The petitioners, having been informed of the alleged passing of an award on 20.05.1997 had obtained information through the Right to Information Act.
This information revealed that an award is said to have been passed on 20.05.1997.
However, no notice of the award was given to any of the petitioners nor was any compensation paid to the petitioners under the said award.

The petitioners also point out to a letter dated 20.04.2000 issued by the District Collector, Krishna District to the Commissioner of land Administration, Andhra Pradesh stating that a draft award had been passed and for the absence of a proper award, it would be appropriate to initiate proceedings of passing of a fresh award.

The petitioners would also contend, on the basis of the information obtained by them, that service of the award has not been effected on the 1st petitioner or of any of the other petitioners and also that the required notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act was not served on the petitioners.
On 11.09.2008 an application of the petitioners for amendment of the writ prayer for the purpose of including a challenge to the award that is said to have been passed on 20.05.1997 was allowed.
While matter stood thus, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the Act, 2013) came into force from 01.01.2014.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In view of the advent of the new Act, the petitioners filed WPMP.No.36299 of 2017 to set aside the land acquisition proceedings initiated against the 69 cents of land on the ground that the proviso to Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 was attracted.

It may also be noted that in November,
2017, the counsel for the official respondents informed the Court that the 1st petitioner namely Sri C. Surya Narayana Murthy had expired and whereabouts of his legal heirs was not known.

After the demise of Sri C. Surya Narayana Murthy, a fresh petition came to be filed by way of W.P.No.34189 of 2022 by one Sri N. Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad who claimed that he had purchased the disputed land from the deceased 1st petitioner and a declaration was sought for declaring the award as being in violation of Section 24 of the Act, 2013.

7. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners both in W.P.No.8542 of 2006 and W.P.No.34189 of 2022 contended that the entire process had fallen foul of the provisions of the Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129136886/
3 Land Acquisition Act, 1894 as well as Section 24 of the Act, 2013.

entities.text: Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 contention of the petitioners is objected by the learned counsel for the respondents.

8. The case of the petitioners, in short, is that Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act requires an award to be passed within two years from the date of publication of the declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.
This declaration came to be notified on 01.06.1995 and an award needed to be passed on or before 01.06.1997.
Since no such award has been passed, the proceedings initiated on 05.07.1994 had lapsed.

In the alternative, even if the draft award of 20.05.1997 is accepted, the land acquisition proceedings would still fail as the requirements of Section 24 of the Act, 2013, namely payment of compensation or taking possession of the acquired land was not available in the present case and as such, the acquisition proceedings would stand lapsed.
9.

The case of the official respondents was that the award proceedings had been completed on 20.05.1997 and necessary compensation payable under the said award had been deposited with the trial Court on 26.04.2006 in terms of Section 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.

It is the case of the official respondents that there were rival claimants for the land before the Land Acquisition Officer,
due to which the Land Acquisition Officer had referred the HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 &
34189 of 2022 said disputes to the trial Court and directed deposit of the compensation with the Civil Court.

Since this was done on 20.04.2006, there has been no violation of the provisions of the land Acquisition Act or the Compensation Act, 2013.
10.
The respondents, apart from the aforesaid defence have also taken the plea that W.P.No.8542 of 2006 is not maintainable any more.

The respondents contend that the 1st petitioner, who is said to be the owner of the land had passed away and no legal heir of the 1st petitioner has come forward,
due to which the writ petition filed by the 1st petitioner has to be treated as abated.

The respondents further contend that petitioners 2 to 9 claim on one hand to be the tenants of the 1st petitioner and on the other hand claim ownership and title over the land by way of some purchase.
The same is clearly contradictory and the respondents contend that the petitioners 2 to 9 have no locus to file the writ petition as their claim, at the highest is that of tenants of the land.
Sri S. Sree Rama Chandra Murthy and Sri M.L. Ali would contend that the petitioners 2 to 9 have been admitted to be the tenants of the land by the 1st petitioner who is the owner of the land.

Once there is such an admission, petitioners 2 to 9 would be entitled to the benefit of a judgment of a full bench of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh in the case of Ushodaya Publications, Hyderabad vs HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad and another1 .

entities.text: Ushodaya Publications, Hyderabad vs HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the lessee of a certain property had sought to challenge the action under the Land Acquisition Act.
This challenge was sought to be denied on the ground that a lessee cannot challenge such acquisition and it is only the owner of the property that could challenge such an acquisition.

The full bench had held that even a lessee would come within the ambit of the term "person interested"
under Section 3(b) of the land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the writ petition of a lessee would be maintainable.

In the light of this judgment, the contention of the respondents that the petitioners 2 to 9 have no locus to file the writ petition has to be Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129136886/
4 negatived.
11.

sentences.text: On the question of lapse of the proceedings, the relevant dates are 05.07.1994 when a notification was published under Section 4(1) and 01.06.1995 when a declaration under Section 6 was published in the local news papers.
Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition reads as follows:

[ 11 -A. Period within which an award shall be made [Inserted by Act 68 of 1984,
Section 9 (w.e.f. 24.9.1984).]

(1)The Collector shall make an award under section 11 within a period of two years from the date of the publication of the declaration and if no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for the acquisition of the land shall lapse: Provided that in a case where the said declaration has been published before the commencement of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act,
1984, the award shall be made within a period of two years from such commencement.
2001 (3) ALD 173 (FB) HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 12.
The award of the Land Acquisition Officer would have to be passed within two years from 01.06.1995, that is an award would have to be passed by 01.06.1997, failing which the entire process lapses.
The official respondents claim that such an award was passed on 20.05.1997, within the period of two years mentioned above.
13. The petitioners dispute the passing of the award on 20.05.1997.
They would contend that no notice of the passing of the award has been given either to the 1st petitioner or to any of the other petitioners.
The award of 20.05.1997 has been described only as a draft award in all official correspondence and therefore, the said award is only a draft award and no award has been passed on 20.05.1997.
Further, compensation would have to be paid upon passing of the award.

However,
no compensation was paid to either the 1st petitioner or to any of the other petitioners. It was only on 23.04.2006 that a sum of Rs.7,67,515/- was sought to be deposited with District Court.

The said amount was sought be deposited in the District Court on the ground that the award dated 20.05.1997 referred to certain disputes relating to title of the land on the basis of which a reference was sought for resolution of these disputes by the District Court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

It is contended that the deposit of compensation after lapse of nearly HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 nine years and the reference to the draft award of 20.05.1997 as a completed award would demonstrate that there was no completed award and it was only a draft award.

The petitioners would also rely upon the letter of the District Collector dated 20.04.2000 in which the District Collector specifically mentioned that the award was a draft ward and it would be appropriate to restart the process and pass a fresh award.
14. The respondents 4 & 5 namely the Chief General Manager, Telecommunications and Divisional Engineer, Telecommunications have filed a separate counter affidavit.
In this counter affidavit, it is stated that the amounts payable towards compensation had been transferred from the Telecommunication Department to the Land Acquisition Officer in 1992 and 1996.

Paragraph No.6 Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129136886/
5 of the said counter affidavit reads as follows:
"I humbly submit that BSNL has followed the appropriate procedure, laid under Land Acquisition Act and acquired the possession of the said site legally by paying the compensation from the public funds and it is unfortunate that land Acquisition Officer has not utilized his good offices to get the petitioners evicted from the said land for the best reason known to him.

entities.text: Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: May be a detailed enquiry like an organisation like CBI is needed to understand why inspite of receiving the compensation several years ago and inspite of repeated letters/reminders addressed to the Land Acquisition Officer he has not taken any action to evict the petitioners.
It is unfortunate that the very Award of the Land Acquisition Officer which was rendered as per the law is jeopardized and the petitioners further filed this writ petition with ill motives.

Hence, it is just and equitable that the petitioners must be evicted from the site, which is acquired by the BSNL, as per law."
HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 15.
This paragraph makes it amply clear that the Telecommunication Department does not have control over the said land and possession remains with the petitioners.
16. The counter affidavit filed by the Revenue Divisional Officer on 24.03.2006 states that the award had been passed by the Land Acquisition Officer-cum-Sub Collector on 20.05.1997.
This award is said to have fixed amount of compensation at Rs.7,67,515/-.
The said amount was also directed to be deposited in the Civil Court as title of the land was not established by the family members of the petitioners as well as the purchasers.

17. On the question of whether the award has been passed on 20.05.1997, the letter of the Collector and District Magistrate, Krishna District, dated 20.04.2000 addressed to the Chief Commissioner of Land Administration is instructive.
In the letter dated 20.04.2000, it is stated that market value proposal submitted by the Sub Collector was approved and marked at Rs.6,77,600/- and the draft award was approved on 28.05.1997.

It is further stated in this letter that an opinion was also obtained from the Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, High Court of Andhra Pradesh on the effect of the order of the High Court dated 24.11.1995 in W.P.No.26001 of 1995.

The learned Government Pleader is said to have opined that the award dated 20.05.1998 can be ignored and HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 fresh proceedings can be initiated after obtaining permission from the Commissioner of Land Revenue.

On this basis, the District Collector had sought permission for passing award after issuing fresh notices under Section 9(3) and 10 as per the directions of the Hon'ble High Court dated 24.11.1995 in W.P.No.26001 of 1995.
It may also be noted that the District Collector has categorically stated that possession of land had not been taken as of 20.04.2000.
This would further strengthen the contention of the Telecommunication Department that the petitioners are still in possession of the land.
18. The contents of the aforesaid letter show that a draft award was prepared on 20.05.1997 and the same was approved on 28.05.1997.

Subsequently, no award had been finalised and permission was Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129136886/
6 sought on 20.04.2000 to ignore the said award and to initiate fresh action.

entities.text: Nerella Venkata Kanaka Durga Prasad vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This would mean that there is no award passed on 20.05.1997.
If such an award had been passed, the question of the District Collector seeking permission for passing a fresh award would not arise.

Similarly the Government Pleader for Land Acquisition having opined that the Land Acquisition Officer would become functus officio after passing of the award would not have advised for issuance of fresh notice and passing an award.
Such an advice would only come in the event of no award having been passed.
A perusal of the award would also show that there is no real discussion on the question of rival claims.
There is cursory mention of such claim and the award states that it was decided to refer it to the Civil Court for decision under Section 30 of the 1894 Act.

The deposit of compensation amount before the Civil Court in the 2006 after a lapse of 8 years after the award is said to have been passed on 20.05.1997 also points to the fact that the said award may not have been passed at all.

20. In the circumstances, this Court has no option except to hold that no award had actually been passed on 20.05.1997 and the award prepared on that date was only a draft award which had been approved on 28.05.1997 but had not been released as a final award after such approval.

In the absence of any award passed before 01.06.1997, the provisions of Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 would apply and all the proceedings initiated under the notification issued under Section 4 of the 1894 Act on 05.07.1994 would stand lapsed.
Accordingly, W.P.No.8542 of 2006 is allowed.
In the circumstances the effect of section 24 of the 2013 Act does not require to be gone into.
21. W.P.No.34189 of 2022 has been filed by a person who claims the land from the 1st petitioner in W.P.No.8542 of 2006.

This writ petition is opposed by the official respondents on the ground HCJ&RRR,J W.P. No.8542 of 2006 & 34189 of 2022 that no such sale could have taken place in view of the fact that the land had already vested in the government and any sale after such vesting is clearly impermissible and invalid.
In view of the fact that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed on 01.06.1997, this contention cannot be accepted.
However, this Court is not going into the question of the validity of the sale between the petitioners in W.P.No.34189 of 2022 and the 1st petitioner in W.P.No.8542 of 2006.
That is a matter to be determined in independent proceedings that may arise or may not arise.

22. In view of the fact that W.P.No.8542 of 2006 has been allowed, there would be no further need for this Court to go into the contentions raised by the petitioner in W.P.No.34189 of 2022 as the acquisition proceedings themselves stand quashed.
23. Accordingly, W.P.No.8542 of 2006 is allowed and W.P.No.34189 is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
